corporations.name: Shipping company
corporations.services: Imports, freight rail, the metro, the skyport and the ports

corporations.name: Arms company
corporations.services: Policing by surveillance (cameras and sensor masts everywhere, squads and drones sent out from the HQ the moment a crime is flagged), prisons and citizen ID

corporations.name: Cybernetics company
corporations.services: The employment office, the island's networks and schooling

corporations.name: Leisure company
corporations.services: Entertainment, hotels, gambling licences and broadcasting

districts.name: The Exchange
districts.notes: Megablocks: each block is one podium of shops and lobbies with two or three towers of smaller companies on it, linked across the streets by skybridges at 40, 100 and 160, so office workers barely touch the ground. Every roof over 180 carries a VTOL or drone pad. Advertising screens face the expressway and Ledger Crossing, and every corporation's colour and mark is on what it runs, down to the bins and lamp posts

districts.name: Exchange Plaza
districts.notes: The hologram pylon at the centre and a screen on each HQ plaza face. The Spine line crosses the plaza on a viaduct at 52, just west of the pylon, with the Exchange Plaza station hanging over the crowd; under the paving a sunken concourse links the four malls and the station stairs

districts.name: Arena Quarter
districts.notes: Between Crown and Ledger Streets, north of the Exchange: the leisure company's arena on its paved forecourt at the head of Exchange Avenue, with a megablock of smaller companies' towers either side, their garden podiums joined to the arena's concourse roof by deck bridges. Screens and banners for the next broadcast event on every face towards the arena; crowds, food stalls and merchandise kiosks on the forecourt on match nights.

districts.name: Old Town
districts.notes: Packed shophouses on crooked lanes. Neon signs and vertical banners hang out over the lanes from both sides until they nearly touch; cable bundles are strung from building to building; AC units, water tanks and antennas crowd every roof. The temple, the wet market and residential lanes south of North Shore Road. After dark Old Market Street, end to end, is the night market: the shophouses along it open as clubs, karaoke halls, arcades, bathhouses, theatres, gaming halls and noodle bars, stalls fill the roadway, the long market hall and the casino face each other along it, and the neon runs unbroken from Stack Avenue to Crown Point

districts.name: Eastgate
districts.notes: Packed tight: continuous street walls 8 to 30 storeys high on a lattice of short streets that jog at every junction and end in T-junctions, so every view closes on a building; alleys built over as passages, and cables, pipes and laundry strung across the streets

districts.name: The Seawall
districts.notes: Apartment towers behind the sea wall; storm shutters on the ground floors, high-water marks on the wall

districts.name: Crown Point
districts.notes: The tallest, most private flats on the island, with the Crown marina below

districts.name: The Warrens
districts.notes: Kowloon-style: tenements built wall to wall into solid masses, 2-block alleys between them, many running as tunnels under upper floors, and a light well in the middle of each mass. Shacks, antennas, pigeon coops and water tanks on every roof; thin bridges between the masses; cables and pipes down every wall; dripping water, bare bulbs, and the neon of the ripperdoc clinics

districts.name: Southside
districts.notes: Mid-rise housing blocks around the unfinished arcology. Under the expressway, the Deck Market: stalls, bars and workshops packed into the deck's shadow, lit by strip lights all day. The vertical farms and the nutrient plant on the east side, the columbarium on the west. Old Shore Road follows the coast as it was before the reclamation: south of it the ground is landfill, north of it the old island

districts.name: The Breakers
districts.notes: Ship-breaking beach: hulks run aground bow first and cut apart, winches hauling plate up the beach to the scrap heaps and the foundry; the breakers live in hull-plate shacks along the shore. Old Shore Road follows the coast as it was before the reclamation: south of it the ground is landfill, north of it the old island

districts.name: The Strand
districts.notes: Waterfront hotels north of North Shore Road, looking over the North Channel. Hotel entrances face the road, terraces face the water; the resort and pier casino anchor the promenade.

districts.name: Broadway
districts.notes: The west-side theatre neighbourhood, from the old Strand to the former Stackside streets. Broadway runs north to south past theatres, cinemas, music halls and restaurants. Backstage lanes hold scene shops, rehearsal rooms and loading doors; apartments stand above the smaller venues.

districts.name: Upper Stack
districts.notes: Stackside relocated to the north-east. Container flats in tidy square rows north of Stack Row, with bolted walkways, laundry, satellite dishes and a gantry crane. The Crosstown and Circle lines serve an open public interchange.

districts.name: Lower Stack
districts.notes: A single salvaged tenement south of Stack Row, grown over Tithe Street and its internal lanes. Workshops and shops line the covered passages; the Circle line passes through the mass and stops inside.

districts.name: Docklands
districts.notes: Corporate docks and cargo warehouses on the reclaimed south-west shore. Ships enter the south-facing berths beneath the shipping HQ; freight leaves towards the southern mainland. Old Shore Road connects the cargo yards to the city.

districts.name: Theatre Square
districts.notes: A paved forecourt for theatre crowds, street performers and outdoor screenings, opening onto Broadway through its east entrance.

roads.name: Old Shore Road
roads.notes: Traces the old coastline: sea wall stones and bollards survive along its south side, and everything south of it stands on reclaimed land

buildings.name: Shipping company HQ
buildings.notes: Covers four south-facing berths. Ships enter from the South Channel; the six-track freight yard crosses above them at 44 blocks, and the freight line leaves through the west wall. Shipping offices and metro control occupy the upper floors.

buildings.name: Salvage dump
buildings.notes: Damaged containers, unclaimed cargo and written-off loads beside the docks. Salvage is carried across the city to Stackside in the north-east.

buildings.name: Yacht club
buildings.notes: Private club for the Crown Point towers: members only, a VTOL pad on the roof

buildings.name: Arms company HQ
buildings.notes: Mall podium filling the north-east quarter. The curved tower above holds everything the arms company runs, so there are no precincts and no patrols: the surveillance centre that watches every camera and sensor mast on the island, the response floors whose squads and drones launch from the roof the moment a crime is flagged, the courts, the prison levels in the windowless core, the armoury, and the citizen ID office in the podium where everyone is scanned and registered. Mast to the ceiling

buildings.name: Leisure company HQ
buildings.notes: Mall podium filling the north-west quarter. The curved tower above is the whole leisure company: the hotel, the casino on the top floors, the broadcast studios that feed every screen on the island, and the licensing office for gambling and entertainment

buildings.name: Pharma company HQ
buildings.notes: Mall podium filling the south-west quarter. The curved tower above holds all of the island's public healthcare: the one hospital (there are no district clinics; emergency drones fly out from its roof), the pharmacy floors of the mall, and the food labs that design what the farms grow; vertical-farm terraces on its faces. Its mall runs straight into the cybernetics company's: one frontage along the plaza's south side. Harbour line Pharma Mall Interchange station is inside, platforms at deck 20

buildings.name: Cybernetics company HQ
buildings.notes: Mall podium filling the south-east quarter. The curved tower above holds everything the cybernetics company runs: the employment office where every worker is assigned, the schools and training floors, the network operations centre for the island's cables and relays, and the private implant hospital with a drone ambulance port on the roof. Its mall runs straight into the pharma company's: one frontage along the plaza's south side. Harbour line Cybernetics Mall station is inside, platforms at deck 20

buildings.name: Hologram pylon
buildings.notes: A slim mast at the centre of Exchange Plaza that projects a rotating hologram (adverts, the news, wanted notices) above the crowd, fed by the broadcast studios in the leisure HQ

buildings.name: Office block
buildings.notes: Podium of shops and lobbies filling the block, one smaller company per tower, linked across the streets by skybridges

buildings.name: Escalator pavilion
buildings.notes: A glass box on the street corner with an escalator up to the podium deck; otherwise the deck is reached through the mall lobbies

buildings.name: Arena
buildings.notes: The leisure company's arena for its broadcast events: a glazed concourse ring with a gate at each end, the Exchange deck reaching its roof by deck bridges, and a dome of cladding panels ribbed with light over stepped seating, a pitch and a screen cube hung from the crown. It faces down Exchange Avenue across its forecourt

buildings.name: Casino
buildings.notes: Licensed by the leisure company: gaming floors stacked under a roof of animated signs, open onto Old Market Street and its stalls at street level, the Spine line passing just over its roof into Old Town North station

buildings.name: Overpass block
buildings.notes: Apartment tower where the East Expressway once ran through its lower floors; flats all the way down now, Relay Street passing its south face

buildings.name: Temple
buildings.notes: The old temple: a courtyard of hanging incense coils behind a gate; the roof ridge carries a neon sign it rents to an advertiser

buildings.name: Wet market
buildings.notes: Low hall of fish, meat and vegetable stalls under strip lights, water running in the gutters

buildings.name: Warrens terminal
buildings.notes: End of the Harbour line: trains come in through the tenements at deck 20 and stop inside, above a ground-floor market; the depot tracks run on to the back wall

buildings.name: Unfinished arcology
buildings.notes: An arcology meant to reach the ceiling, abandoned when its developer went under: finished floors to about 60, then bare concrete frame, then steel to 176 with a tower crane still standing on top. Squatters live in the finished floors; the frame above is open to the wind. Spine line Arcology station is inside, platforms at deck 52

buildings.name: Vertical farm
buildings.notes: Stacked grow floors under purple light, glass on every face; the crops go by conveyor to the nutrient plant next door

buildings.name: Vertical farm

buildings.name: Nutrient plant
buildings.notes: Where the farms' crops and imported bulk become the island's cheap food: paste, bars and cartons stamped with the pharma company's mark

buildings.name: Columbarium
buildings.notes: A vertical cemetery: niches for ashes stacked floor after floor, rented by the decade; the lease runs out and the niche is emptied. Candles and small screens with the faces of the dead

buildings.name: Beached hulk
buildings.notes: A feeder ship run aground bow first for scrapping; cutters work it from the stern in, and the plate goes up the beach on winches

buildings.name: Cable landing station

buildings.name: Skyport
buildings.notes: VTOL and drone port: pads on the roof, hangars below; aerodynes fly from here to the rooftop pads on the towers
